data.title: bn-2npu (continues cr-10mg1y rounds 1-4): C018 TCB audit, checker mutation lane, eventuality scope kernel fix

data.body:
[HIGH] TCB-02 misses  source redirection.

Failure mode: A checking crate can compile an unscanned file that exposes a verdict from decoded input. This defeats the wire-only entry invariant.

Edge cases: A dummy standard module file satisfies lines 691-692. A true  condition redirects rustc to the hidden file.

Rollback: Remove the new fail-closed claim, or reject conditional path attributes before merging.

Monitoring: The current covenant and TCB audit both report clean, so existing gate output cannot detect this bypass.

Validation: I used an in-memory Tree overlay. It added a conditional path redirect, a dummy standard module, and a hidden non-wire . Both  and  returned no findings.

Fix the attribute scan or bind the audit to rustc's actual module inputs. Add a compiling fixture with the dummy standard module present.
Correction: the omitted identifiers are cfg_attr(all(), path = PATH), decide, rule_no_dynamic_loading, and rule_wire_bytes. The complete reproduction result was KCOV [] and TCB02 [].

data.reason: HIGH: TCB-02 misses cfg_attr path redirection, which can hide a non-wire verdict entry from both covenant scans.

data.body: Verified fixed at b2d96f58236f2d848cd59e103aebdbe86e52558d. tools/check_kernel_covenant.py:699-704 bans multiline cfg_attr path redirects. tools/check_tcb_audit.py:862-920 compares rustc dep-info inputs with scanned inputs. The compiling redirect fixture records the expected mismatch.

data.reason: The target bans cfg_attr path redirects and binds scanned files to rustc dep-info inputs.

data.body:
[HIGH] TCB-02 ignores callable public statics.

Failure mode: A checking crate can expose a public static dyn Fn that accepts &crate::wire::Certificate and calls the private checking functions. This returns Verdict from decoded input and defeats the claimed wire-only entry boundary.

Edge cases: items() inventories a public static, but lines 783-790 skip every kind except fn and method forms. fn_tokens() matches lowercase fn, not the Fn trait or a closure. The per-crate authority tests also search only pub fn and pub const fn. The source digest and dep-info equality still pass because rustc and the scan both see the file.

Rollback: Remove the universal fail-closed claim, or reject callable public const/static/field/associated-const forms. A rustc-derived public API surface is safer than extending this lexical grammar.

Monitoring: Current covenant and TCB evidence report one verdict entry per crate, so existing gate output does not reveal this bypass.

Validation: I used an in-memory Tree overlay that appended pub static DECIDE_DECODED: &(dyn Fn(&crate::wire::Certificate) -> Verdict + Sync) with a closure calling check_finite_closure/check_state_type. After adding the generated inventory line, rule_wire_bytes returned no findings.

Add a compiling fixture for this callable-static form and make both TCB-02 and the authority test reject it before merge.

data.reason: HIGH: tools/check_tcb_audit.py:783 ignores callable public statics, so a decoded-certificate-to-Verdict closure can pass TCB-02 and the authority tests.
The original public-static bypass is repaired at fb5287e. A distinct public trait-associated constant bypass has its own thread.

data.body:
[HIGH] TCB-02 skips callable associated constants on public traits.

Evidence: tools/check_tcb_audit.py:789 only scans declarations containing `pub `. Rust trait members omit visibility. Lines 885-886 then skip every `trait-item`. The copied authority scan has the same gap at crates/continuum-certificate/tests/inv004_no_self_certification.rs:478-518.

Failure mode: A public trait can declare `const DECIDE: &dyn Fn(&Certificate) -> Verdict`. A checking-base implementation can bind it to a private decision function. Callers then obtain a decoded-input verdict producer while TCB-02 reports one wire-only entry.

Edge cases: Required or default associated constants, `FnMut` or `FnOnce`, qualified `Certificate` paths, and implementations on public zero-sized holder types all bypass this branch.

Rollback: Remove the fail-closed TCB-02 claim, or inspect callable and verdict-bearing associated constants in public traits and their implementations.

Monitoring: Current TCB-02 output, Rust authority tests, and retained C018 evidence can all stay green for this route.

Validation: An in-memory Tree overlay added this public trait, a public holder implementation, and every generated inventory line. `rule_wire_bytes` returned `[]`. Add a compiling fixture and require both TCB-02 and each Rust authority test to reject it.

data.reason: HIGH: TCB-02 and the Rust authority scans accept a public trait-associated callable constant that exposes a decoded-certificate Verdict producer. See tools/check_tcb_audit.py:789 thread.

data.body: [HIGH][RESOLVED BY SCOPE] At target 7d18ec94492bcb9265fbe4b793d137d750f59cec, the technical miss remains: tools/check_tcb_audit.py:473-474 classifies a public trait constant as trait-item, and tools/check_tcb_audit.py:896-897 skips it. The target now treats this as an explicit qualification RED. tools/check_tcb_audit.py:33-46 and notes/plan/docs/18_CLAIMS_MATRIX.md:188-205 state that TCB-02 is incomplete. tools/tcb-audit/fixtures/tcb02-trait-associated-const.json:1-23 records the route. tools/check_tcb_audit.py:1633-1641 pins that the scan still accepts it. C018 remains TARGET, and the current checking-base source contains no such route. Failure mode: a future trait-associated callable can bypass both scans while the gate stays green. Edge cases: required or default associated constants, FnMut or FnOnce, qualified Certificate paths, and public holder implementations. Rollback: keep C018 unqualified and remove the partial audit if its explicit RED cannot be preserved. Monitoring: retain the known-miss field, fixture compilation result, authority-test false result, and TARGET claim. Validation: the committed fixture compiles, and the evidence records that both TCB-02 and the authority test accept it. This resolves the review blocker through explicit scope correction, not through a technical fix. The separate risk:critical human gate remains required.

data.reason: Target 7d18ec scopes TCB-02 to named forms, records the bypass as a known qualification RED, keeps C018 at TARGET, and contains no current trait-associated verdict route.

Reviewed the full persisted range 24f134c57add4535b079a86db391988f6b4867bf..7d18ec94492bcb9265fbe4b793d137d750f59cec. The temporal eventuality fix, package-identity checks, compiled-input binding, evidence validation, and TCB public-value repairs are sound on static inspection. The trait-associated callable route remains an explicit qualification RED, C018 remains TARGET, and no current checking-base source uses that route. No security blocker remains. This LGTM does not satisfy or bypass the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.

data.body: Kernel review (GOV 4, second non-author reviewer). Soundness: every goal-avoiding execution stays in the goal-stopped scope. A finite one ends at an in-scope empty row, which stuck_state (check.rs:494-501) refuses as ProgressDeadlock. An infinite one has its inf-often set inside one in-scope SCC, which fair_cycle refuses. Initial goal states are marked and not expanded. No false rejection: post-goal dead ends and cycles are out of scope. Pre-goal branches stay in scope because only goal states skip expansion (check.rs:363-365). Resources: iterative DFS, O(V+E), after decode under MAX_STATES and MAX_TRANSITIONS. Mutants in a scratch copy: removing the goal stop fails 3 lib tests, 3 c018_checker_mutation tests and 2 differential tests. Disabling stuck_state fails 3 lib tests, 5 c018 tests and 1 differential test. Other kernel crates change docs and tests only. Non-blocking note 1: CheckedClaim::reachable_states now counts goal-stopped states for FairSccExclusion (verdict.rs:310-318). This is documented, but consumers that read it as full reachability change meaning. Non-blocking note 2 (pre-existing): executions are maximal paths of the carried relation. Stutter at a non-terminal state is not modelled, which matches the RFC 0015 terminal-stutter policy. No soundness defect found.

data.reason: Kernel review, second non-author reviewer (GOV 4). Goal-stopped reachability plus the in-scope dead-end check is sound and complete for eventually-goal under weak fairness over the carried relation. Tests pass and both reverts are caught by the lib, c018 mutation and differential lanes. Other kernel crates change docs and tests only.
